title: French Republican Calendar
intro: A revolutionary French calendar that began at the autumn equinox in 1792, with differently named months and ten-day groupings called decades.
summary: Twelve months of thirty days, plus five or six complementary days. Year I starts on 22 September 1792.
origin: Adopted during the French Revolution, the Republican Calendar was officially used from 1793 until 1805. Its epoch marks the founding of the First Republic.
structure: Each of twelve months has thirty days organised into three ten-day decades. Five or six complementary days finish the year.
pattern_note: Extra days fall outside the twelve regular months. The software extends the dates by an explicit arithmetic rule beyond the years when the calendar was used.
history: The Revolutionary government renamed months after seasonal and agricultural themes and replaced the familiar seven-day week with a ten-day rhythm within each month.
example: 22 September 1792 in the historical Gregorian-to-Julian context is the epoch for 1 Vendémiaire, Year I, in this calendar model.
limits: After its historical use, this implementation follows a shifted-Gregorian leap convention, not the full Romme proposal or an assertion that people kept using it. The software's arithmetic continuation must not be confused with historical dates.
